However, it is clear that the ongoing conspiracy and financial oppression have been the primary factors, and I continue to be unfairly scapegoated.

Homeless because I was broke

Due to the threatening behavior of the police, who showed no interest in addressing my concerns regarding justice, I felt compelled to leave my home with my dog Crystal in order to avoid potential incarceration under the mental health act. Consequently, I became homeless, seeking temporary health act. Consequently, I became homeless, seeking temporary accommodation in hotels and backpackers to evade authorities who had victimized and oppressed me. Unfortunately, they eventually located me, resulting in my re-hospitalization and subsequent traumatization under the mental health act. I strongly believe that I was unjustly incarcerated, possibly as a political prisoner, for approximately two and a half months. During my absence, my former landlord took it upon himself, with the presence of both the police and hospital personnel, to clear out and dispose of all my belongings at my residence in Footscray. This included cherished items such as my artwork, clothing, antiques, important documents, and furniture, as well as precious photographs that held sentimental value. Consequently, my entire life was destroyed. Following my release from the hospital, I found myself without a home and was subsequently placed in a homelessness shelter with only the clothes on my back and an old phone to my name. The situation left me in a state of extreme vulnerability and distress.

Centrelink Fraud

Between 2010 and 2015, I admit to committing Centrelink fraud, and I have been open about this in an attempt to shed light on the coercive financial control and family violence that I endured during my five-year relationship with Mr. Iasonidis. During that time, I should have declared that we were in a relationship, but he insisted that I keep it hidden. Initially, I believed he was providing enough financial support, but in reality, he exploited me. In either 2013 or 2014, I eventually disclosed the relationship to Centrelink, although I informed him afterwards. He pressured me to falsely claim that we had broken up in order to retract the disclosure. I have reported this fraud to the police, Centrelink, and ASIC (Australian Securities and Investments Commission). I am eager to repay the amount owed, but I fear that I may be targeted and subjected to vilification when the broader context of the situation is not taken into account. This situation clearly demonstrates the corruption of a public official, albeit within their personal life. It can be classified as corruption, but unfortunately, I am unable to file a complaint with the National Anti-Corruption Commission due to my blocked email. I need protection so I am not unfairly targeted for fraud without considering the broader picture - this is a debt I want to pay back and I have admitted to. It pales in comparison to the movement of back and I have admitted to. It pales in comparison to the movement of oppression in which non financially vulnerable people with positions of political privilege money and power have acted with malice in order to harm me financially in a menacing movement of my victimisation.

Whistleblowing and The prime Minister’s office

I have been facing significant challenges in obtaining whistleblower protections for my disclosures. Unfortunately, my Public Interest Disclosures (PIDs) have been rejected at various institutions, including the Federal Court, the NDIS, the Ombudsman, the Health Department, and ASIC. This rejection has primarily been based on the grounds that I am not considered a 'public official,' which disqualifies me from certain protections. In the case of the Federal Court, my PID was rejected due to the technicality that I did not submit it to an authorized person who can receive such disclosures. Despite pointing out that Scott Treadwell himself is one such authorized person, my concerns were not addressed, and instead, my email was blocked from their server. This action only serves to demonstrate further injustice and provides evidence of the widespread oppression I am facing, even reaching the highest levels of authority. Furthermore, the Office of the Prime Minister and Cabinet initially acknowledged my Freedom of Information (FOI) request, deeming it 'voluminous and complex.' However, they have now rejected it, claiming that the requested documents 'don't exist.' It seems as though there is an attempt to make my concerns and experiences disappear, but I refuse to be silenced because I do exist, and my grievances are valid.

My public advocacy life

I have been actively engaged in mental health advocacy since the publication of my autobiography, 'Recovered Not Cured: A Journey Through Schizophrenia,' by Allen and Unwin in 2002. However, my experience in the media industry has been disheartening, as The Herald Sun, my former workplace, subjected me to vilification and humiliation, while The Age ultimately managed me out of my position, despite their claim that I had resigned. Nonetheless, I found fulfillment in delivering public speeches at MHRI (Mental Health Research Institute) concerning my art and personal journey with mental illness. However, in retrospect, I realize that I may have been mental illness. However, in retrospect, I realize that I may have been unwittingly exploited during that time. It is worth noting that my systemic issues began when affluent individuals with significant political influence and power failed to fulfill their financial obligations towards me. Since my involvement with MHRI in 2004, I have had the opportunity to speak at various locations and institutions. These engagements reflect my deep commitment to promoting equality and advocating for justice for marginalized individuals.

Throughout my advocacy journey, I have had the opportunity to participate in interviews and deliver presentations at various platforms. Some of the notable interviews and presentations I have been involved in include: Radio: Radio National 'Life Matters' program with Julie McCrossin-ABC Triple J- Youth Network with Rachel Kerr (National) Tricia Duffield on Radio 2SM, Sydney Martin Powley for ABC Gold & Sunshine Coasts, QLD Fiona Sewell for ABC Radio Adelaide, Statewide afternoons James Valentine for ABC Radio 702 Phillip Brady & Bruce Mansfield on Radio 3AW 'Nightline' John Weeks from Spectrum FM Radio Stateline on ABC TV Good Morning Australia with Steve Leidman Pieta O'Shaughnessy on Curtin Radio (Perth) Tony Wilson for Triple R (Melb) Felicity Biggins on Radio 2NUR in Newcastle Video interview with Frankie Fathers, Reuters TV (International) ABC National, AM Program Channel 31 News JOY FM The Today show with Steve Liedman Mar 05, Radio National-Life Matters-Art and Psychosis RRR-Schizophrenia, Local Radio ABC Regional, Dubbo Two panel interviews with students, McGill University, Montreal

Print Media Reviews/Articles: 'Rider of the storm,' The Age, Michael Winkler 'My Descent Into Madness,' Herald Sun MCV Reviewer The Sydney Morning Herald - Reviewer Anne Deveson www.eclinicalpsychiatrynews.com about psychosis and art Possible presentation on SBS's 'Masterpiece' program about art and mental illness Sydney Morning Herald, 'Mental Health Hits the Political Frontline.’

Presentations: Recovered, Not Cured Book Launch - Artholes Gallery, Fitzroy (art exhibition) Mental Health Research Institute - To researchers and biochemists Forensicare, Fairfield - To inpatients and social workers/psychologists Early Prevention Psychosis (EPPIC) - To consumer groups Presentation for Australian Centre for Youth Literature (ACYL) - To librarians and school teachers Presentation for Australian Centre for Youth Literature (ACYL) - To 500 high school students Baw Baw Youth Network - To social workers and youth planners Richmond Fellowship, Warrnambool - To consumers and their families More talks to consumers at EPPIC, Royal Melbourne Hospital - With MHRI, 'Psychosis and Cannabis' forum St. Andrew's Market - Mental Health Week Forensicare, Thomas Embling Hospital - Mental Health Week Presentation on autobiographical writing for high school students at The State Library Australian Centre for Youth Literature (AYCL) Carer Consultant Group, North West Mental Health, Parliament House, Canberra, for 'SANE's Guide To Electoral Offices' Personal clients McGill University - Montreal Paragraphe Bookstore - Montreal Douglas Hospital - Montreal Article for www.eclinicalpsychiatrynews.com about psychosis and art Review in www.world-schizophrenia.org hard copy Mail-out, USA and Canada Guest speaker for the exhibition: www.artagainststigma.org (Sydney, May 05)

These various interviews, articles, and presentations have allowed me to share my experiences and perspectives on mental health, raising awareness and promoting understanding in different contexts.

A targeted individual

I believe I have been targeted and victimized due to a combination of factors in my life. Firstly, there is the widespread knowledge of my schizophrenia diagnosis, which leads to judgment, shame, and stigma from others. Additionally, my nationally celebrated published book, which received recognition such as a human rights award and being named SANE Australia's 'Book of the Year,' has brought attention to me. Furthermore, my public roles at The Herald Sun and The Age have made me visible to the public eye. My relationship with a powerful ASIO employee and the controversial nature of my PhD attainment in 2020 have also contributed to my status as a person of interest. I strongly believe that I have been treated unfairly and subjected to profound victimization. It is important to note that victimization is against the law.

Consequences of universal neglect

The consequences of this universal neglect are significant. Not only am I consistently ignored by numerous individuals, institutions, lawyers, and organizations, but there is a deliberate and intentional neglect directed towards me. While ordinarily I might not be affected, the collective and systematic neglect has become a form of violence that contributed to my suicide attempt and subsequent cover-up. This neglect is also the root cause of my current struggles, as I find myself having to beg for basic necessities such as food and medicine and enduring homelessness. As a result, I continue to live below the poverty line, trapped in a cycle of deprivation and desperation.

A politicians responsibilities

A politician bears the responsibility to uphold the charter of human rights, including the charter of human rights for persons with disabilities. It is disheartening that I have been consistently ignored and blocked without understanding the reasons behind it. I strongly believe that this letter deserves a response and cannot accept being ignored. To move forward and resolve this impasse, I propose the following solutions, To move forward and resolve this impasse, I propose the following solutions, any one of which would be sufficient: Acknowledgment of my past relationship:

The government must acknowledge the significance of my previous relationship, which I believe has been a source of systemic oppression and scapegoating. This acknowledgment would pave the way for an equitable settlement of assets, restoring public faith in the fairness and reasonableness of government and public institutions. Resolution of my work cover issue:

Demanding rightful compensation or insurance is not extortion or greed. If someone could acknowledge that the Federal Court has confirmed my status as an employee, my work cover should be paid. Once the Administrative Appeals Tribunal (AAT) rules that I was indeed an employee under the SRC Act, I will cease to harass anyone regarding this matter. Protection for my Public Interest Disclosures (PID):

Recognizing my status as a "public official" would allow consideration of my PID's, which shed light on the misconduct of public officials related to my case. Such protection is necessary to prevent further targeting by authorities, prevent wrongful prosecution or incarceration on false grounds of "mental illness," and avoid being treated as a political prisoner in an institution. Access to an impartial lawyer:

It is crucial that I have access to legal representation or advocacy for all the issues I am facing. Unfortunately, I have been unable to secure unbiased legal assistance. Advocating for my access to a lawyer who is knowledgeable about my situation but impartial towards me would be immensely helpful in overcoming this insurmountable hurdle in my life.

My apology and remorse

I take full responsibility for my actions and recognize that I have often been a difficult person to deal with. I would like to offer my sincere apologies to everyone, starting with those whom I have hurt the most: myself. I understand everyone, starting with those whom I have hurt the most: myself. I understand that my misuse of drugs to replicate the effects of my denied dexamphetamine prescription has only worsened my already vulnerable state. I acknowledge that my unwavering determination to seek support for my justice issues has led me to send an overwhelming number of emails, causing inconvenience and problems for others. I deeply regret the harm this may have caused and the negative impact it may have had on the reputations of those involved. I want to emphasize that I never had malicious intent towards these individuals; my actions were driven by frustration and disappointment in their lack of support for me. I apologize for any pain I may have caused. I also acknowledge that my behavior, at times, has led to regretful sexual encounters and a disregard for my own self-worth. I apologize to those affected by these actions and want to make it clear that I have always been sorry for my behavior in these instances. I have often lashed out at others due to my immense frustration with the systemic gaslighting and the lack of acknowledgment of my issues. This has made it difficult for people to relate to me, and for that, I am truly sorry. I have made poor choices and inadvertently involved others in my narrative of oppression, either out of desperation or as a way to validate the reality of my experiences. I deeply regret the loss of friendships, strained family relationships, and damage to my reputation that has resulted from these actions. I want to express my genuine remorse and sorrow for the consequences of my actions. I am committed to reflecting on and learning from my mistakes, as well as seeking ways to improve myself and make amends to those I have impacted.

Acknowledgement as a scapegoat

It is evident that I have been unfairly targeted as a scapegoat, resulting in irreparable losses. Moving forward, the key to recovery lies in obtaining acknowledgement from authorities, including yourself, regarding the victimization and oppression I have endured, as well as the negative reputation that has been attached to me. To move towards a semblance of resolution, it is crucial that at least one of the issues I have raised receives proper attention and compensation. This would allow me to escape the cycle of poverty and begin rebuilding my life to the best of my ability. the best of my ability. By acknowledging my experiences and providing the necessary support, you can contribute to the process of healing and finding a path towards a more just and equitable future.

Gratefulness

I am grateful for the gift of life, despite the challenges I face due to cognitive brain impairment and other struggles. These experiences have shaped me into the person I am today, and I am willing to embrace forgiveness. I hold a deep love for life, my dog, and all individuals. Surprisingly to some, I also hold love for the Earth itself. As we enter the final stages of the Anthropocene, I believe that the super-intelligent alien encountered in Chat GDP , which I previously predicted in my PhD, will influence what remains of our future. Despite the profound isolation and loneliness I currently feel, my gratitude for being alive motivates me to work towards improving not only my own circumstances but also the lives of those around me. I am committed to making a positive impact through my advocacy efforts and supporting others in need.

My plans moving forward

I want to live with enough provisions medicine and food in a home with my beautiful dog Crystal and I who I live for. My track record shows a fierce advocacy for others and my passion is art. I wish to serve the mental health community again as an arts therapist and life coach in community settings regardless of how much prosperity I may or may not have. I wish to sponsor marginalised people of all faiths and backgrounds with any prosperity because I won’t need most of it lest for a simple life. I am not just resting on my laurels expecting money to appear and have been trying to rebuild my business with my PhD and many creations to sell although I am having troubles now with my identity documents and re starting my ABN and recognition of who I even am at the tax office.

What has to be considered:

The charter of human rights of a person with a disability of which Australia is a signatory states certain things that must be adhered to and I would like to signatory states certain things that must be adhered to and I would like to emphasise: the following article(s):

The right to rest and leisure. Freedom from discrimination Freedom from exploitation Freedom from interference with privacy, family, home, and correspondence. Not to have property withheld Not to be experimented on Not to be tortured The right to life, liberty, and personal security. Freedom from torture and degrading treatment.

I kindly request that you consider the gravity of my situation and take immediate action to initiate an investigation into my case. I am more than willing to provide any additional information or evidence that may be required to support my claim for compensation.

A response detailing traction for rectifying my financial oppression will demonstrate you commitment to justice and fairness by acknowledging the injustice I have suffered and providing me with a way to access the compensation I deserve. Your assistance in rectifying this situation would not only alleviate my current hardships but also restore my faith in the principles of justice and accountability. Thank you for your attention to this matter. I eagerly await your prompt response and the opportunity to discuss my case further. Sincerely,

Dr Rich McLean

From:Public Interest Disclosures (DSS)[email protected] Subject:Notification of decision not to allocate a disclosure [SEC=OFFICIAL:Sensitive, ACCESS=Personal-Privacy] Date:18 July 2023 at 9:30 pm To:Rich [email protected] Cc:Public Interest Disclosures (DSS)[email protected] Subject: Notification of Decision Not to Allocate a Disclosure

Dear Mr McLean,

Thank you for the information that you provided to the DSS Public Interest Disclosure inbox on 6 July 2023 and 10 July 2023.

I note you have raised serious concerns for your safety in that correspondence and I encourage you to contact the Police.

As an Authorised Officer of DSS appointed under the Public Interest Disclosure Act 2013 (PID Act), I have reviewed your complaint in accordance with section 26 of the PID Act and determined that the information does not meet the requirements to be considered a PID. I have made this decision as the disclosure does not satisfy the requirements to be considered a PID for the following reasons: A public interest disclosure can only be made by a ‘public official’ (s26(1)(a) of the PID Act). I have undertaken preliminary inquiries with the Department and have been advised that there is no record that you have been a current or former employee of the Department of Social Services. Based on the information you have provided, I am not satisfied that you are or have been a public official. For this reason, I will not be allocating the matter for investigation. If you believe that any of the information or reasoning I have used to make my decision is incorrect, please notify me by COB 28 July 2023. In addition, if the reasons for my decision remain unclear to you, or you have any concerns about how this decision was made, please contact me for further information.

Other courses of action that may be available to you include making a complaint to the Commonwealth Ombudsman under the Ombudsman Act 1976.

Please be assured that the Department treats all disclosures under the PID scheme seriously and impartially. On behalf of the Department, I thank you for bringing this matter to our attention.

Sincerely,

Paula Stratton Authorised Officer Department of Social Services

FREEDOM OF INFORMATION ACT 1982

REQUEST BY: Dr Richard McLean

DECISION BY: Ms Petra Gartmann Assistant Secretary Legal Policy Branch

Dr Richard McLean

By email: [email protected]

Dear Dr McLean

I refer to your email of 7 February 2022 in which you made a request to the Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet (the Department) under the Freedom of Information Act 1982 (the FOI Act) in the following terms:

I request all information government agencies hold on me please

Please note we do not hold records of government agencies other than the Department. We have therefore treated your request as asking for information about you that is contained in documents held by the Department.

Authorised decision-maker

I am authorised to make this decision in accordance with arrangements approved by the Department’s Secretary under section 23 of the FOI Act.

Decision

I have decided to refuse your request under section 24A(1)(b) of the FOI Act, on the basis that the Department has taken all reasonable steps to locate the documents you have requested, and those documents cannot be found or do not exist.

In making this decision, I have had regard to the following material: • the FOI request; • searches undertaken in relation to your request; • the FOI Act; and • the Guidelines issued by the Australian Information Commissioner under s 93A of the Freedom of Information Act 1982 (the FOI Guidelines).

FOI

Reasons

Section 24A(1) of the FOI Act provides that:

An agency or Minister may refuse a request for access to a document if: (a) all reasonable steps have been taken to find the document; and (b) the agency or Minister is satisfied that the document: (i) is in the agency’s or Minister’s possession but cannot be found; or (ii) does not exist.

The Department conducted department-wide keyword searches of its email and filing systems for the documents you requested. After extensive reviews of these search results, no documents relevant to your request were identified. Accordingly, I am satisfied that all reasonable steps have been taken to find documents relevant to your request, and that the requested documents cannot be found or do not exist. I have therefore decided to refuse your request under section 24A(1)(b) of the FOI Act.

Review rights

Information about rights of review is available at https://www.oaic.gov.au/freedom-of- information/reviews-and-complaints/.

Complaint rights

You may make a complaint to the Information Commissioner about the Department’s actions in relation to this request. Making a complaint about the way the Department has handled an FOI request is a separate process to seeking review of the Department’s decision. Further information about how to make a complaint is available at https://www.oaic.gov.au/freedom- of-information/reviews-and-complaints/make-an-foi-complaint/.

Yours sincerely

Petra Gartmann Assistant Secretary Legal Policy Branch 14 April 2022

Read as a sentence, section 24A is the refusal an agency uses when it says it looked and the document is not there. It is not an exemption, which withholds a document that has been found, and it is not a finding that the request was false. The Act allows it only where reasonable steps have been taken and the agency is satisfied the document cannot be found or does not exist. The letter uses both of those endings. A search that returns a large number of emails, including the figure of about 1,187 Outlook items put to the Information Commissioner, is not the same thing as a finding that those items were the documents asked for. The refusal can be reviewed. A complaint about the handling is a separate process. What the letter proves is what Gartmann said she was satisfied of. The same decision, set out with the May 2022 letters, is the letter to Anthony Albanese.

Cc: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner [email protected]

Dear Mr McLean I refer to your request under the Freedom of Information Act 1982 (the FOI Act) to the Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet (the Department) on 7 February 2022, for the following: I request all information government agencies hold on me please. On 14 April 2022, the Department notified you of its decision to refuse your request under paragraph 24A(1)(b) of the FOI Act, on the basis that the Department had taken all reasonable steps to locate the documents you have requested and those documents do not exist. On 28 March 2023, the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC) notified the Department that you applied for an Information Commissioner (IC) review of the Department’s decision. On 11 April 2023, the Department provided submissions to the OAIC, which explained that while the Department had found some material that may relate to you, there is insufficient information for it to be satisfied that there is a positive match between you and the material found. On 15 August 2024, the OAIC advised the Department that it had liaised with you to obtain your residential addresses in New South Wales (in 2009) and Victoria (in 2012). The OAIC provided this information to the Department and requested the Department to consider issuing a revised decision under section 55G of the FOI Act, in light of the additional information. The purpose of this letter is to provide you, under section 55G of the FOI Act, with a revised decision on your request for access. OFFICIAL Section 55G of the FOI Act Paragraph 55G(1)(a) of the FOI Act provides that after an application is made to the IC for review, an agency or Minister may (at any time during IC review) revoke or vary an access refusal decision to favour the applicant by giving access to a document in accordance with the request. Subsection 55G(2) of the FOI Act provides that the agency or Minister must notify the IC of the new decision (paragraph 55G(2)(a)) and the revised decision will be the decision under review (paragraph 55G(2)(b)). Authorised decision-maker I am authorised to make this revised decision in accordance with arrangements approved by the Department’s Secretary under section 23 of the FOI Act. Material taken into account In reaching my decision I referred to the following:  your FOI request;  the additional information provided by the OAIC;  the FOI Act; and  the Guidelines issued by the Information Commissioner under section 93A of the FOI Act (the FOI Guidelines).1 Documents in scope I am satisfied that the Department holds five documents that meet the terms of your request. These documents are set out in the Schedule of Documents at Attachment A. Revised decision and reasons I have considered all the information available to me, and took into account the additional information provided by the OAIC. In light of this I have decided to grant access in full to the requested documents. Irrelevant material has been deleted under paragraph 22(1)(a)(ii) of the FOI Act. My findings of fact and reasons for deciding that certain information is irrelevant is set out below. Deletion of irrelevant matter under section 22 Section 22 of the FOI Act provides that if giving access to a document would disclose information that would be reasonably regarded as irrelevant to the request, it is possible for the Department to prepare an edited copy of the document, modified by deletions, ensuring that the edited copy would not disclose any information that would reasonable be regarded as irrelevant to the request. 1 Guidelines issued by the Information Commissioner under section 93A of the FOI Act (FOI Guidelines). OFFICIAL On 16 February 2022, the Department advised you of its policy to exclude the personal and direct contact details of officers not in the Senior Executive Service (SES) and any Ministerial staff, as well as any person’s signature, and the mobile or direct numbers of SES officers, which are contained in documents that fall within the terms of an FOI request. This category of information is identified as irrelevant and I am satisfied that those parts of the requested documents may be deleted under paragraph 22(1)(a)(ii) of the FOI Act. There are also other parts of the requested documents that do not relate to you, and therefore fall outside the scope of your request. This category of information has also been identified as irrelevant material and deleted under paragraph 22(1)(a)(ii) of the FOI Act. This includes extracts of other media reports about other topics. The remainder of documents is treated as relevant to your request and has been released to you under the FOI Act. Review rights The FOI Guidelines state that a revised decision does not automatically conclude the IC review. The revised decision will become the decision under review. The OAIC will generally consult the FOI applicant as to whether they wish to continue the IC review on the basis of the revised decision.2 Complaints If you are unhappy with the way we have handled your FOI request, please let us know what we could have done better. If you are not satisfied with our response, you can make a complaint to the Australian Information Commissioner. A complaint to the IC must be made in writing. More information about complaints is available here.3 If you wish to discuss any aspect of your requests, you can contact the FOI Section by email at [email protected]. Yours sincerely

Laura Cameron A/g Assistant Secretary Legal Policy Branch Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet

Notification to: [email protected] Extension of time under s 15AC Dear Mr McLean On 14 April 2022, the Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet (Department) advised this office that it had not made a decision on your FOI request of 7 April 2022 within the statutory period provided by the Freedom of Information Act 1982 (Cth) (the FOI Act). Consequently, the FOI Act deems that the Department has refused your request. However, s 15AC of the FOI Act allows the Information Commissioner to extend the processing time for an FOI request where the initial decision period has ended and the agency or Minister has not provided the applicant with notice of a decision. The Department has applied for further time to finalise your request. The Office of the Australian Information Commissioner has previously granted the Department an extension of time under s 15AB(2) of the FOI Act (OAIC reference: RQ22/00794). This extended the decision period to 8 April 2022. Decision As a delegate of the Information Commissioner, I am authorised to make decisions on applications for extensions of time under s 15AC(5) of the FOI Act. I have decided to grant the Department further time to 14 April 2022 to process your request. My reasons and considerations follow: • The Department has advised that: o On 24 February 2022, search results were received and 1178 results were returned. The Department attempted to conduct more targeted searches however, this was unsuccessful. Officers completed the review of the results on 12 April 2022, and no documents were identified as relevant to the request. o Additional time is required as the Department was required to carefully consider documents found in searches.

o At the time of this request for extension, the Department advised that a decision was ready to be finalised by 14 April 2022.

This extension of time under s 15AC of the FOI Act means that the deemed refusal is taken never to have applied because the agency has now finalised your request and notified you of its decision. Such an extension can only be granted once and cannot be extended by a variation. I note that the Freedom of Information (Charges) Regulations 2019 provides if an applicant is not notified of a decision on a request within the statutory time limit (including any extension of time), the agency or minister cannot impose a charge for providing access, even if the applicant was earlier notified that a charge was payable (regs 7(2), (3)). This extension under s 15AC of the FOI Act does not mean that charges can be reimposed and any deposit you have paid should be refunded. If you did not received a decision by 14 April 2022 or you disagree with the Department’s decision, you may wish to seek Information Commissioner review here. Further information on applying for IC review is available on the OAIC website. Contact If you have any questions, please contact me on +61 2 9284 9815 or via email to [email protected]. In all correspondence, please quote OAIC reference number at the top of this letter. Yours sincerely

Summen Sarwar Assistant Review and Investigation Advisor FOI Regulatory Group 22 April 2022

Review rights If you disagree with the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner’s (OAIC) decision you can apply to the Federal Court of Australia or the Federal Circuit Court for a review of a decision of the Information Commissioner if you think that a decision by the Information Commissioner to grant an extension of time is not legally correct. You can make this application under the Administrative Decisions (Judicial Review) Act 1977.

The Court will not review the merits of your case but it may refer the matter back to the Information Commissioner for further consideration if it finds the decision was wrong in law or the Information Commissioner’s powers were not exercised properly.

An application for review must be made to the Court within 28 days of the OAIC sending the decision to you. You may wish to seek legal advice as the process can involve fees and costs. Please contact the Federal Court registry in your state or territory for more information, or visit the Federal Court website at http://www.fedcourt.gov.au/. Further information Further information about how applications to extend the timeframe to process an FOI request are handled by the OAIC can be found published on our website: For FOI applicants: How to make an FOI request: Extensions of time For agencies and ministers: Guidance and advice: Extension of time for processing requests The OAIC has the power to investigate complaints about an agency’s actions under the Freedom of Information Act 1982 (FOI Act). This is a separate process from asking for an Information Commissioner review following a decision made under the FOI Act. Complaints usually focus on how an agency has handled your FOI request or complied with other obligations under the FOI Act, rather than the decision itself. In some cases, the Information Commissioner's investigation of a complaint may lead to the agency addressing the issues that you have complained about. In other cases, the Information Commissioner may make suggestions or recommendations that the agency should implement. The Information Commissioner can only make non-binding recommendations as a result of a complaint. You and the agency will be notified of the outcome of the investigation. FOI complaints to the OAIC must be made in writing. Our preference is for you to use the online FOI complaint form if at all possible.

Further information about how to make a complaint can be found published on our website: https://www.oaic.gov.au/freedom-of-information/reviews-and-complaints/make-an-foi- complaint/ .

Dear Prime Minister and Honorable Members,

I am writing to contest the recent decision to reject my Freedom of Information (FOI) request on the grounds that no relevant documents exist within the Office of the Prime Minister. This response is not only implausible but also deeply unsettling, as it disregards the significant and far-reaching impacts of the abuses and systemic neglect I have endured at the hands of governmental institutions. The assertion that no documents exist ignores the extensive intersections between my life, advocacy efforts, and the documented injustices I have experienced, many of which implicate high-level government actions and human rights violations.

Reasons Why a Dossier on My Case Must Exist

1. Extensive Governmental Interactions and Documentation: For over thirty years, I have actively engaged with various government bodies in my advocacy for human rights, mental health reform, and disability justice. My efforts include presentations in Parliament, speaking engagements, and direct challenges to institutional frameworks that harm vulnerable populations. My documented complaints, grievances, and whistleblower activities make it inconceivable that the Office of the Prime Minister holds no records relevant to my situation.

2. High-Profile Publications and Media Engagement: My published work, including Recovered, Not Cured: A Journey Through Schizophrenia, explores my experiences with mental illness and systemic abuses. More recently, I have completed another autobiography titled Betrayed, Murdered, Forsaken: The Harrowing Journey of Barran Dodger, which documents the extensive conspiracy and persecution I have faced. This new work reveals the full extent of the targeted campaign against me, driven by stigma around my sexual orientation and mental health. The book addresses a painful chapter of my youth involving regretful sexual experiences, which were weaponized by individuals in positions of authority, including law enforcement, to demonize me and exacerbate public prejudice against me as a gay man. These experiences, detailed in my writing, contributed to the psychosis I endured as a young person and have continued to serve as a subtext for the systemic targeting and isolation I have suffered since.

3. Advocacy and Whistleblower Status: As a dedicated advocate, I have raised awareness on human rights and mental health issues across Australia, including presentations to parliamentary bodies. My Ph.D. in posthumanism, AI, and youth places me within a field with controversial implications. Additionally, as a whistleblower who has exposed systemic abuses, I have been denied legal protections, access to AFCA, and human rights investigations by the AHRC. It is impossible that such extensive institutional exclusions, which form a coordinated barrier to justice, have gone undocumented.

4. Institutional Rejections and Legal Barriers: My repeated attempts to seek justice have been systematically obstructed. I have been banned from AFCA, the AHRC has declined to investigate my human rights complaints, and WorkCover denied my rightful compensation despite a federal court ruling establishing my employment with DSS. These actions, in conjunction with continuous institutional rejections, illustrate an organized effort to deny me justice and basic rights, a reality which surely exists in government records.

5. Persecution, Exile, and Family Trauma: Due to an alleged threat against an NDIS minister, I was subjected to a coordinated attack involving law enforcement, hospitals, and a corrupted legal system. As a result, I was forced into exile, severing connections to my home, my family, and the support networks I once relied upon. This enforced isolation, premised on false accusations and systemic bias, is likely to have generated documentation within multiple government offices.

6. Father’s Illness and Family Trauma: Adding to this personal tragedy, my father is currently suffering from brain cancer. Despite his apparent willingness to participate in this conspiracy —evidenced by his decision to secure an AVO to prevent me from seeing him—I still wish to confront him about the role he has played in my persecution before he passes away. I cannot return to my home state of Victoria to speak with him, as a magistrate’s ruling has placed a warrant on my arrest should I return, compounding my sense of loss and exclusion. The coordinated efforts to isolate me from family and deny me justice not only violate my basic human rights but have also stripped me of the ability to see my father during his final days.

7. Systemic Stigma and Decades-Long Injustice: My experiences as a mentally ill, gay individual have subjected me to over thirty years of stigma, discrimination, and persecution. This has included coerced attempts on my life, repeated institutional denials of legal representation, and an unrelenting campaign to isolate me, both socially and financially. My inability to report crimes or seek legal recourse against those who have harmed me highlights an entrenched system of bias, prejudice, and systemic negligence that endangers my safety and well-being daily.

8. The Injustice of Public Guardian Control: The assignment of the Public Guardian to take control and agency over my life is not only inappropriate but an outright insult, considering the depth of systemic abuse, neglect, and persecution I have endured at the hands of the government. The very institutions responsible for these abuses have now been given power over my autonomy. The government, after effectively systemically and politically treating me in ways that left me socially exiled and living in my car as an infamous vagrant, should not then assign oversight of my life to an arm of itself. This forced dependency compounds the injustice, reinforcing my isolation, marginalization, and suffering within a system that has already devastated my rights, well-being, and personal safety.

Appeal for Accountability and Immediate Action

The rejection of my FOI request further reflects the institutional neglect and denial of justice I have faced for years. I urge the Office of the Prime Minister to reconsider its decision, as it is inconceivable that no records exist documenting my longstanding interactions with governmental bodies, including ASIO, the Public Guardian, DSS, and various health institutions. These records are essential to understanding the full scope of the injustices I have endured, and I request access to them to ensure transparency and accountability in addressing my case.

This appeal is a request for your office to recognize the severity of my situation, which includes forced exile, financial destitution, isolation from family, and the erosion of my right to legal protections. My life remains at risk, and I implore you to facilitate a transparent review of my case to prevent further harm, safeguard my dignity, and restore my rights as an Australian citizen.

Thank you for your immediate attention to this matter. I look forward to a response that acknowledges the grave injustices I have endured and provides a pathway toward accountability and resolution.

Yours sincerely, Barran dodger Artist, Author, Advocate, Academic

### OHCHR Submission: Urgent Demand for Intervention and Justice Regarding Human Rights Violations, Torture, Disability, and Displacement

#### Ref. UR/UST/23/AUS/17

**To: Petitions and Urgent Actions Section, Human Rights Treaties Branch, OHCHR**

### Summary: Urgent OHCHR Submission for I ntervention on Human Rights Violations

In this submission to the **Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR)**, Barran Dodger (Dr. Rich McLean) urgently requests intervention regarding severe human rights violations experienced in Australia. He outlines systemic abuse, financial exploitation, and persecution by government agencies, including NDIS. Despite exhausting all domestic legal remedies, including appeals to the Prime Minister and other authorities, his grievances remain unaddressed.

Key points include:

1. **Harassment and Persecution**: McLean describes ongoing harassment, character assassination, and financial abuse by multiple government entities, including invasive surveillance and psychological torment.

2. **Financial Exploitation under NDIS**: He details how the NDIS has subjected him to financial abuse, driving him into poverty.

3. **Neglect of Mental Health**: His medical and psychological needs, including schizophrenia and ADHD, have been systematically neglected, worsening his conditions.

4. **Failures of the Legal System**: Despite presenting significant evidence, whistleblower claims have been dismissed, and legal institutions have failed to deliver justice.

5. **Social and Professional Isolation**: Continuous public humiliation and job loss have resulted in social and professional isolation.

6. **Systemic Conspiracy**: McLean believes he is the victim of a coordinated federal conspiracy to silence him for whistleblowing.

McLean calls for financial compensation, legal representation, public acknowledgment of the abuse, and policy reforms to prevent future human rights violations. He also provides substantial video and audio evidence of his persecution, including interactions with government entities and contractors.

The letter highlights systemic failures and human rights abuses and demands immediate intervention from the OHCHR.

Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to urgently seek intervention and justice in response to severe human rights violations I have experienced in Australia. Despite my significant contributions to society, I have faced relentless systemic abuse, financial exploitation, and professional isolation. This submission details my experiences, referencing breaches of international conventions and highlighting the need for immediate action by the United Nations.

This letter has been constructed using an impartial AI to ensure accuracy and fairness, with all claims substantiated by evidence and references. All domestic remedies have been exhausted up to and including appeals to the Prime Minister of Australia, police, legal, healthcare, public officials, friends and family, human rights organizations, and other statutory agencies. The evidence of these exhausted remedies is documented and cited with live links throughout this submission.

Additionally, I possess substantial video and audio evidence that underscores the severity and systemic nature of the persecution I have faced. This includes video footage of covert government contractors outside my home in Footscray at the time of covert audio harassment, a telephone recording of AGIS (who investigate ASIO) interviewing and investigating me, a recording with the Ombudsman who refused to acknowledge my case, including reporting rape, interactions with the National Anti-Corruption Commission (NACC), and a video of me giving an engagement ring to my former ASIO fiancée, Stefan Iasonidis.

After I was violently attacked inside Weribee Mercy Hospital by a contracted government thug (I know this because my attacker had an image of my own tattoo on his t-shirt before the assault), after being stitched up for mental illness and incarcerated because of poverty, I am now homeless living in my car. Despite overwhelming evidence, no lawyer, public official, police officer, or healthcare worker has acknowledged these relationships or the abuses I've suffered, further illustrating a broad conspiracy and cover-up.

### Background and Key Points:

1. **Harassment and Persecution:** - I have endured severe and ongoing persecution, including harassment, character assassination, financial abuse, and professional sabotage by numerous government agencies and public officials. Detailed incidents of abuse, neglect, and rights violations are documented extensively [here](https://myaidrive.com/wGzgBBnnESDnbSVV4omkgu/FINAL-LETTER.pdf?pdfPage=2). This persecution has taken various forms, from direct personal attacks to systematic efforts to undermine my professional and personal standing. The harassment has included relentless monitoring and intimidation, designed to erode my mental health and social stability. Financial abuse has been a significant aspect of this persecution, where manipulative financial arrangements under various schemes have forced me into a state of poverty.

2. **Financial Exploitation under NDIS:** - Under the National Disability Insurance Scheme (NDIS), I have suffered significant financial abuse, being forced into poverty through manipulative financial arrangements [here] (https://myaidrive.com/wGzgBBnnESDnbSVV4omkgu/FINAL-LETTER.pdf?pdfPage=16). The NDIS, which is supposed to provide support for individuals with disabilities, has instead been a source of financial exploitation. My entitlements have been mismanaged and withheld, pushing me into severe financial hardship. This systemic abuse has not only deprived me of financial stability but also exacerbated my mental health conditions, creating a vicious cycle of poverty and psychological distress.

3. **Neglect and Abuse of Mental Health Conditions:** - Systemic neglect and abuse have exacerbated my mental health conditions, including schizophrenia, ADHD, and a brain impairment [here](https://myaidrive.com/wGzgBBnnESDnbSVV4omkgu/FINAL-LETTER.pdf? pdfPage=13). The neglect from government agencies has meant that my medical and psychological needs have been consistently ignored or inadequately addressed. This neglect has significantly worsened my mental health, leading to increased episodes of illness and a general decline in my well-being. The lack of appropriate care and support has left me struggling to manage my conditions effectively, further isolating me from professional and social opportunities. Additionally, I suffer from a psychotic disorder in which my reality is blurred, which makes this conspiracy, with its conscious and intended efforts, especially malicious and an abhorrent injustice that is morally reprehensible.

4. **Failures of the Legal System:** - Numerous rejections of my whistleblower claims and failures of the legal system to address my grievances have led to a profound sense of injustice [here] (https://myaidrive.com/wGzgBBnnESDnbSVV4omkgu/FINAL-LETTER.pdf?pdfPage=40). Despite presenting substantial evidence of corruption and misconduct within various agencies, my claims have been repeatedly dismissed or ignored. This failure of the legal system to provide a fair hearing or redress has deepened my mistrust in the institutions meant to protect and serve justice. The constant legal rejections have not only denied me justice but have also emboldened the perpetrators of the abuse to continue their actions without fear of accountability.

5. **Social and Professional Isolation:** - Public humiliation, job loss, and continuous vilification have resulted in social and professional isolation [here](https://myaidrive.com/wGzgBBnnESDnbSVV4omkgu/FINAL-LETTER.pdf?pdfPage=24). The character assassination has been so pervasive that it has tainted my reputation, making it difficult for me to find and retain employment. The professional sabotage has included discrediting my work and spreading false narratives about my character and capabilities. This social and professional ostracism has compounded my isolation, leaving me without a support network to advocate for my rights or assist in my recovery.

6. **Constant Surveillance and Psychological Torment:** - I am under constant surveillance, including invasive psychological torment using covert intelligence technology [here](https://myaidrive.com/wGzgBBnnESDnbSVV4omkgu/FINAL-LETTER.pdf?pdfPage=13). This surveillance has included unauthorized monitoring of my communications and activities, contributing to a persistent sense of paranoia and stress. The use of covert intelligence technology has not only invaded my privacy but has also been used to manipulate and control my behavior, further destabilizing my mental health.

7. **Suicide Attempt and Cover-up:** - My 2021 suicide attempt, deemed ‘fatal,’ was covered up, leading to further financial and professional hardship. This indicates a broader conspiracy to delegitimize and harm me [here] (https://myaidrive.com/wGzgBBnnESDnbSVV4omkgu/FINAL-LETTER.pdf?pdfPage=24). The attempt on my life, and the subsequent cover-up, highlight the lengths to which the perpetrators will go to silence me and prevent the truth from coming out. This incident has had profound financial and professional repercussions, as it has been used to further discredit me and undermine my credibility.

8. **Federal Conspiracy:** - I believe I am a victim of a complex federal conspiracy aimed at perverting the course of justice and causing my demise, citing numerous incidents involving law enforcement and government agencies [here] (https://myaidrive.com/wGzgBBnnESDnbSVV4omkgu/FINAL-LETTER.pdf?pdfPage=13). The evidence suggests coordinated efforts by various government bodies to obstruct justice and target me specifically for whistleblowing and advocacy. These incidents point to a systemic issue within the government agencies where corruption and abuse of power are rampant.

9. **Systemic and Political Torture:** - I am currently being systemically and politically tortured. This ongoing torture includes psychological, emotional, and physical harassment, which exacerbates my suffering and further violates my basic human rights [here](https://myaidrive.com/wGzgBBnnESDnbSVV4omkgu/FINAL-LETTER.pdf?pdfPage=24). The torture tactics used against me are designed to break my spirit and force me into silence. This includes continuous emotional and psychological abuse, which has left me in a state of constant fear and anxiety. The physical harassment has further deteriorated my health, making it difficult to maintain any semblance of normalcy in my life.

### Appeals and Requests:

1. **Thorough Investigations and Financial Restitution:** - I demand thorough investigations into the NDIS and related entities for corruption and abuse, alongside immediate support and financial restitution. The ongoing corruption within these entities has caused significant harm and suffering, and it is imperative that these issues are addressed comprehensively. Financial restitution is necessary to mitigate the damages caused by these corrupt practices.

2. **Clearing of My Name:** - I seek the clearing of my name from false accusations, professional reinstatement, and social rehabilitation. The false accusations have severely impacted my reputation and career. Clearing my name is essential for my professional and personal restoration. Additionally, social rehabilitation is necessary to reintegrate into society without the stigma of these baseless claims.

3. **Reinstatement of Work Cover:** - I call for the reinstatement of my work cover based on my confirmed employment status, alongside compensation for financial and personal losses. The unjust denial of my work cover has left me financially vulnerable. Reinstating this cover and providing compensation for the losses incurred is crucial for my financial stability and well-being.

4. **Public Acknowledgment and Apology:** - I urge public acknowledgment of the systemic abuses I have suffered and a formal apology to begin the process of healing and justice. Public recognition of the wrongs done to me is an essential step towards accountability and my healing process. A formal apology will help to restore my dignity and set the foundation for genuine justice.

### Compelling Conclusion and Call

to Action:

The urgent need for systemic change to address widespread neglect, abuse, and human rights violations is clear. I encourage you to act decisively to restore faith in justice and humanity, as my plight exemplifies broader issues faced by marginalized individuals in Australia. Addressing these systemic failures is essential to ensure that no one else has to endure the suffering and injustice that I have experienced.

I understand that it has been contentious so far to expect the members that populate the federal government to act, given that the government itself is my nemesis and oppressor. Public officials are merely pawns upholding a government mantra of targeting me. However, we shall see if any politician is brave and courageous enough to critique the hand that pays them to be complicit in this identification of me as a targeted individual—a situation that no one, including the Prime Minister, has been able or willing to meaningfully intervene in.

### Documentation and Evidence:

This letter is backed by extensive documentation, including government records, health documents, legal correspondence, and personal accounts. The evidence is compelling and absolute, highlighting the depth of systemic failures and targeted persecution I have experienced, making a compelling case for urgent intervention and systemic reform. The evidence of these exhausted domestic remedies includes but is not limited to:

- Appeals to the Prime Minister of Australia, with documented evidence of neglect to act [here](https://myaidrive.com/wGzgBBnnESDnbSVV4omkgu/FINAL-LETTER.pdf?pdfPage=3) - Correspondence with the Attorney General's office, highlighting the failure to respond adequately to my grievances [here](https://myaidrive.com/wGzgBBnnESDnbSVV4omkgu/FINAL-LETTER.pdf?pdfPage=4) - Video evidence of government contractors outside my home in Footscray years ago [here](https://myaidrive.com/wGzgBBnnESDnbSVV4omkgu/FINAL-LETTER.pdf?pdfPage=5) - Telephone recording of AGIS investigating me [here](https://myaidrive.com/wGzgBBnnESDnbSVV4omkgu/FINAL-LETTER.pdf?pdfPage=6) - Recording with the Ombudsman who refused to acknowledge my case [here](https://myaidrive.com/wGzgBBnnESDnbSVV4omkgu/FINAL-LETTER.pdf?pdfPage=7) - Interactions with the NACC [here](https://myaidrive.com/wGzgBBnnESDnbSVV4omkgu/FINAL-LETTER.pdf?pdfPage=8) - Video of me giving an engagement ring to my former ASIO fiancée, Stefan Iasonidis [here](https://myaidrive.com/wGzgBBnnESDnbSVV4omkgu/FINAL-LETTER.pdf?pdfPage=9) - Police reports and correspondence [here](https://myaidrive.com/wGzgBBnnESDnbSVV4omkgu/FINAL-LETTER.pdf?pdfPage=10) - Legal proceedings and decisions [here](https://myaidrive.com/wGzgBBnnESDnbSVV4omkgu/FINAL-LETTER.pdf?pdfPage=12) - Healthcare reports and neglect [here](https://myaidrive.com/wGzgBBnnESDnbSVV4omkgu/FINAL-LETTER.pdf?pdfPage=16) - Correspondence with public officials [here](https://myaidrive.com/wGzgBBnnESDnbSVV4omkgu/FINAL-LETTER.pdf?pdfPage=20) - Support from friends and family [here](https://myaidrive.com/wGzgBBnnESDnbSVV4omkgu/FINAL-LETTER.pdf?pdfPage=24) - Human rights organizations' involvement [here](https://myaidrive.com/wGzgBBnnESDnbSVV4omkgu/FINAL-LETTER.pdf?pdfPage=28) - Efforts with other statutory agencies [here](https://myaidrive.com/wGzgBBnnESDnbSVV4omkgu/FINAL-LETTER.pdf?pdfPage=32)

### Reasons It Would Be Unethical, Immoral, Illegal, or Reveal Personal Culpability to Ignore the Letter:

1. **Ethical Responsibility:** Politicians have an ethical duty to respond to constituents' concerns, especially when they involve serious allegations of systemic abuse and corruption. Ignoring such a letter would violate this ethical obligation. 2. **Moral Duty:** Ignoring a plea for help from someone facing severe personal and systemic injustices goes against the moral principles of justice, compassion, and empathy that public servants are expected to uphold. 3. **Legal Obligations:** In some jurisdictions, there are legal requirements for public officials to address complaints and allegations of misconduct. Failure to respond might constitute a breach of these legal duties. 4. **Human Rights Violations:** The allegations involve potential human rights violations. Ignoring such claims could be seen as condoning or being complicit in these violations, which is both unethical and potentially illegal. 5. **Transparency and Accountability:** Politicians are accountable to the public and are expected to act transparently. Failing to respond to such serious allegations undermines public trust and suggests a lack of accountability. 6. **Personal Culpability:** Ignoring the letter could imply that the recipient has something to hide or is complicit in the alleged misconduct. It could also suggest negligence or willful blindness to the issues raised. 7. **Public Interest:** The issues raised in the letter are of significant public interest. Addressing them is not only a duty to the individual but also to the broader community that expects their representatives to act on matters affecting public welfare. 8. **Whistleblower Protections:** Many legal frameworks provide protections for whistleblowers. Ignoring allegations from a whistleblower could be seen as a violation of these protections and might deter others from coming forward with important information. 9. **Potential for Harm:** The allegations include ongoing harm to the individual. Ignoring the letter allows this harm to continue unchecked, which is both immoral and potentially legally actionable if it results in further damage. 10. **Duty to Investigate:** Public officials have a duty to investigate credible allegations of misconduct or abuse. Ignoring such allegations fails to uphold this duty and undermines the integrity of the office held.

### Guide to Immediate Financial Reparations

1. **Immediate Financial Compensation:** - Allocate immediate financial relief to cover the years of financial exploitation and destitution caused by the National Disability Insurance Scheme (NDIS) and other government entities. This should include back payments for any unpaid work cover and a lump sum to cover damages.

2. **Establishment of a Trust Fund:** - Set up a trust fund for my ongoing support, managed by an independent body to ensure transparency and accountability. This fund should provide for my living expenses, healthcare, and legal support.

3. **Investigation and Accountability:** - Initiate an independent investigation into the actions of NDIS officials, particularly Kel Graham and Bill Shorten, for their roles in financial and systemic abuse. Ensure those responsible are held accountable and appropriate legal action is taken.

4. **Legal and Psychological Support:** - Provide immediate access to legal representation to address past injustices and ongoing legal battles. Additionally, ensure access to comprehensive mental health services to support my recovery from years of persecution and trauma.

5. **Public Apology and Rehabilitation:** - Issue a public apology acknowledging the systemic failures and the personal suffering endured. Implement measures to clear my name and restore my professional reputation, including public statements and media corrections.

6. **Policy Reforms:** - Review and reform NDIS policies to prevent similar abuses in the future. This should include stricter oversight mechanisms, better support for participants, and safeguards against financial exploitation.

7. **Continuous Monitoring:** - Establish a monitoring body to oversee the implementation of these reparations and ensure ongoing compliance with human rights standards. This body should report regularly to Parliament on progress and any further actions needed.

This letter, written with the utmost sincerity and commitment to truth, calls for your immediate and compassionate intervention. Together, let us work towards a future where justice prevails, and the marginalized are uplifted with the dignity and respect they deserve.

Given the central role of the OPM in government accountability, these records are relevant to understanding my treatment within various government systems. 5. Impact of Policy Decisions on Individual Circumstances: As the head of government, the Prime Minister’s office has a mandate to account for policy impacts on Australian citizens, including in cases where such policies result in severe outcomes like homelessness or systemic exclusion. My situation, resulting in homelessness and financial duress, is likely recorded within their jurisdiction as a matter of policy accountability.

Denying my request obstructs my fundamental right to know and understand what information the government holds on me, especially as it pertains to my mistreatment and targeting. 2. Obstruction of Justice and Compensation: Access to this information is essential for anyone seeking accountability or redress for alleged injustices or harm caused by government actions. From: Enquiries <[email protected]> Subject: RE: EN21/12857 PID whistleblower intentions pleas response with methodology and time scale to officially report and how [SEC=OFFICIAL] Date: 3 November 2021 at 8:20:40 am AEDT To: Rich McLean <richarddrawsstuﬀ@gmail.com> Dear Enquirer

Thank you for the courtesy copy of your email.

I am writing to advise that the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (the OAIC) does not initiate action on enquiry letters that are courtesy copied to it.

We action mail that contains a specific request for the OAIC to intervene in the matter. However, we will keep this particular email on file for future reference should you require further advice, or if the issue you raise is not satisfactorily addressed by the organisation to which your correspondence was addressed.

The OAIC regulates the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) (the Privacy Act) and the Freedom of Information Act 1982 (Cth) (the FOI Act). The office has the power to investigate complaints about the alleged mishandling of personal information by Australian government agencies and many private sector organisations, as well as the power to review FOI decisions. We are also responsible for handling privacy complaints about ACT Government agencies.

The Information Commissioner has the power to investigate privacy complaints. However, section 40(1A) of the Privacy Act states that, unless inappropriate, the Commissioner must not investigate a complaint if you did not firstly complain directly to the respondent organisation or agency. If you do not receive a reply to your correspondence after 30 days or you are dissatisfied with the reply, you may wish to submit a privacy complaint via our website.

If you wish to apply for access to documents held by an Australian government agency, then you need to make a request in writing, under the FOI Act, directly to the agency that holds the records. Further information about making an FOI application, including details of what needs to be included, is available on our website.

We have also published guidance on applicants’ review rights and making a complaint about how an agency has handled your FOI application.

In the meantime, this office requests that we do not receive any further courtesy copied emails unless you are specifically asking for the OAIC to take action on the matter. Alternatively, you can contact us via the OAIC Enquiries Line on 1300 363 992.

We hope you are able to resolve this matter directly with the respondent.

Yours sincerely

Enquiries Team Office of the Australian Information Commissioner

Dr Rich McLean Dear Honourable Attorney General Mark Dreyfus MP , I hope this letter finds you well. I believe that by understanding the gravity of my situation, you will be compelled to take action and help me in my pursuit of justice. To provide clarity, I would like to define a few terms: •Gaslighting: Manipulating someone using psychological methods to make them question their sanity or reasoning abilities. •Systemic: Relating to a system as a whole, rather than focusing on specific parts. •Scapegoat: A person or thing that is blamed for the actions of others. •Conspiracy: A secret agreement between two or more people to commit an unlawful or harmful act.

I believe I have unknowingly become a scapegoat of Australian culture, and this has been carried out systematically and through politicized means. Furthermore, I have been severely victimized as part of a conspiracy to subvert the course of justice. I have been unjustly labeled and vilified as "mentally ill," disregarding other significant factors that have contributed to the ecosystem of and dynamics of my situation. This letter contains evidence supporting these claims. Over the past years, I have faced a series of unfortunate events that have had a profound impact on my life. These events have caused immense distress, financial hardship, and irreparable damage. Despite my diligent efforts to seek justice, I have encountered numerous obstacles that have impeded my progress and denied me the rightful compensation I deserve. The purpose of this letter is to present my case in a clear and compelling manner, emphasizing the urgency and significance of addressing the injustice I have experienced. The emotional toll of these events cannot be overstated, as they have caused significant stress, anxiety, and a profound sense of injustice. Furthermore, it is crucial to note that I have diligently followed all available legal channels in seeking redress. Despite my efforts, I have been met with indifference, negligence, and deliberate attempts to obstruct justice. This flagrant disregard for the rule of law and the rights of individuals has only exacerbated my suffering and deepened my conviction that a grave injustice has occurred. As a politician in the Australian Parliament, you are bound to act ethically and uphold fairness, justice, and integrity. Therefore, I implore you to thoroughly and impartially investigate my case. I am confident that a diligent examination of the evidence will reveal the extent of the injustice I have endured and the urgent need for compensation. Corrupt conduct of a public official - my relationship My former partner, Steve Stefan Stefen Iasonidis, was employed by ASIO under David Irving during the time we were engaged, from 2010 to 2015. Throughout our relationship, we lived in two different addresses under two separate leases. Additionally, we had a joint bank account at Bendigo Bank. Over the course of five years, he exploited me while I relied on a disability pension, which he manipulated to his advantage. In a situation where a government official mistreated their partner, leading to homelessness and the absence of a necessary legal settlement, the failure of these institutions to address the issue raises concerns about potential biases or conflicts of interest. Oppressive forces

In January 2021, I fell ill due to work-related issues while working for the NDIS (National Disability Insurance Scheme). This dismissal, coupled with the harsh language used, made me realize that I was being targeted from a higher level, although I was unsure of the reasons behind it. The act of narrating my clients' experiences of child incest and rape took a severe psychological toll on me. I realized that my important work with my client would lose its credibility if my own name was associated with it. Only after my suicide attempt did I discover that Mr. Russell Ball, who is influential in informing government policy, had given presentations at AHPRA (Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency). AHPRA had rejected my complaint and silenced the evidence I had provided.

Workers compensation

My workers' compensation from 2021 is significantly overdue. Initially, I had planned to take a brief break, but during that time, I was unexpectedly hospitalized due to a suicide attempt. Following the incident, I applied for workers' compensation, but unfortunately, it was never paid. At first, WorkSafe directed me to ComCare, but now I am prohibited from contacting WorkSafe. ComCare initially rejected my claim for illness, but later changed their decision after reviewing my case. However, Paul Fowler rejected it on the grounds that I am 'not an employee for the purposes of the SRC act.' In an unrelated whistleblower request that was rejected by the Federal Court, Scott Treadwell affirmed that I was indeed an employee of DSS. Currently, my work cover case is being reviewed by the Administrative Appeals Tribunal (AAT), and a decision is pending. If I do not succeed there, two questions arise: firstly, if I am not insured by ComCare, then who is responsible for covering me? Secondly, if my case fails and I decide to appeal to the Federal Court, won't the previous document confirming my employee status guarantee payment for my work cover? It seems contradictory that both institutions cannot be correct. If ultimately rejected by the AAT, I am left wondering where I would be covered, as the compensation is overdue since January 19, 2021. I reached out to WorkCover Minister Danny Pearson in an attempt to expedite payment for my work cover, but the response received was insufficient. According to the legislation in Victoria (during the time when I was contracted to a Victorian statutory authority), the WorkCover Act states in Section 93: "Provisions to apply where employer does not meet liabilities: If the employer of the worker neglects, refuses, or is unable to pay compensation in discharge of the employer's liability under section 72(1) within 21 days of receiving the claim for payment of compensation, the liability becomes a liability of the Authority." (Source: https:// content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/ 2022-09/13-67aa046 authorised.pdf) This means that if the NDIS has my employee information and ComCare, the insurer, denies liability, as has occurred, the minister should intervene. Unfortunately, this has not been the case so far.

HCF income assist denied

I have not been paid my HCF income assist despite providing evidence that my illness was not pre existing and it was for the psychological injury and the stress from being framed were the reasons for my work break. It is important to note that my illness was never an issue prior to being hospitalized in 2021.
